items.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021
items.q: you know Billy Joel to Bruce Springsteen, Madonna, Prince, Michael Jackson

ctx.x: Is jazz a hard sell these days more than it used to be? It’s never — it’s been a long time since it was sort of the popular music of the day, but I wonder as time goes by if people’s attention span and their listening habits make it harder to sort of sell jazz.

I think it’s live music of all kinds have been affected across the board, from the top down. From the most popular pop stars, you know, down to the semi-professional, or semi- amateur solo folk guitarist. I think it’s — live music has been affected across the board. And I don’t know if it just has to do with advances in technology, the internet, but I mean I think of in the 80s even Madison Square Garden, Giants Stadium, pop stars would fill — you know Billy Joel to Bruce Springsteen, Madonna, Prince, Michael…
whoever, would fill 50,000 seat stadiums regularly. And I don’t think that exists for them anymore either.
